items.question: Which candidate vanilla quest/event has a verifiable player-level gate, and at which transition is the gate evaluated?

hypotheses.model: A candidate gate is evaluated at a single event or quest-start transition.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: A controlled trace would show the level predicate on one transition, and alternate initiation routes would not evaluate it.

hypotheses.model: The candidate gate is checked repeatedly or at a later alias, dialogue, or encounter transition.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: A trace would show later or repeated level-dependent checks, with different intermediate states after an alternate route.

items.next_action: Select a named candidate from authorized dated source material, then verify its prerequisite against the winning record in the complete active AE order.

items.question: Can a player-available alternate initiation path reach a representative gated quest/event without console or plugin intervention?

hypotheses.model: Every valid initiation path applies the same gate before the event begins.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: The vanilla candidate path and ordinary path both stop at the same gate under the same level and baseline.

hypotheses.model: At least one player-accessible event path reaches a distinct initiation point before that gate is evaluated.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: A clean level-one sequence starts the real event while preserving level and without forced stage changes.

items.next_action: After Q-0001 identifies a verified gate, enumerate distinct entry paths and state the observation that separates H1 from H2.

items.question: What event and native-use path awards armor skill XP from an incoming hit, independently of armor protection?

hypotheses.model: Armor skill XP is credited on a hit event after protection/damage is computed.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: The award path is reached only after a validated incoming-hit event and can be separated from armor rating.

hypotheses.model: Armor skill XP is credited through a distinct event/use route whose prerequisites are not identical to damage calculation.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: Native/control traces show a separately gated skill-use call while protection remains effective.

items.next_action: Review retained source/protocol knowledge and define independent hit, damage, armor-rating, skill-XP, and character-XP observables before seeking a matching binary.

items.question: Can a vanilla-reachable state preserve functional worn armor while suppressing armor skill XP credit from verified incoming hits?

hypotheses.model: Protection and skill XP share an inseparable prerequisite in the candidate scenario.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: Any state suppressing XP also removes or changes the verified armor protection or hit event.

hypotheses.model: Protection computation and skill-XP credit have a separable vanilla-reachable condition.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: A verified hit still receives armor protection while measured armor XP remains unchanged and normal XP returns in control.

items.next_action: Use Q-0003 to identify distinct protection and award observables; do not test a bypass until a real hit and functioning armor can be independently verified.

items.question: How does enchanting credit and round skill XP, and can a useful enchantment be crafted below the relevant 15→16 or 20→21 XP threshold?

hypotheses.model: The operation grants skill XP according to a quantized or rounded function of enchantment inputs.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: Boundary-adjacent inputs yield repeatable steps or discontinuities in raw skill XP.

hypotheses.model: The operation grants a smooth/cumulative amount whose displayed skill level hides the threshold crossing.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: Raw XP changes before the displayed level changes, and cumulative controls expose the threshold.

items.next_action: Define input values, raw skill-XP observables, threshold baselines, and controls; treat ULP/rounding explanations as hypotheses until raw representations are recorded.

items.question: Which transitions determine potion/poison ActiveEffect duration, lifetime, and persistence across save/load?

hypotheses.model: The observed effect is one ActiveEffect whose lifetime is extended or fails to expire.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: The same effect instance/reference survives waiting, travel, save/load, and recalculation without reapplication.

hypotheses.model: The apparent persistence is replacement, reapplication, or another permanent ability/enchantment.
hypotheses.predicted_discriminant: Instance identity, source, or remaining duration changes at a transition while the displayed magnitude persists.

items.next_action: Define instance identity, duration, magnitude, dispel, save/load, and reapplication observables that distinguish one surviving ActiveEffect from replacement.
